title: North Star: can you see what it's thinking?
blurb: The whole course as one night walk across a torn-paper map of 14 Saturdays, while a sealed mind egg slowly turns to glass. Ends with a tappable map of every week.

title: Which way is down, and how big a step?
blurb: A paper hiker on a real loss surface: SGD zig-zags, learning rates too small and too big, momentum as a heavy marble, Adam's two running averages. Then race all three yourself.

title: Every shape has a story
blurb: A night-shift librarian sorts 24 paper tiles into a (2, 3, 4) tensor, flattens it with einops, unrolls a VHS batch, stretches stamps by broadcasting, matchmakes an einsum, and fires a batch of rays at a wall. Then drive the tiles and the torch yourself.

title: Who gets the blame?
blurb: A paper factory on the night shift: a plane carries 1.5 forward through ×w, +b, tanh and a squared error until the bell rings. Then rewind the Walkman and watch the blame relay backwards, station by station, summing where the line splits. Then drive x, w, b and the target yourself and check backprop against wiggling.

title: The little window that learned to see
blurb: A red paper View-Master window hunts for a cat in an 8x8 Game Boy picture: real multiply-and-sum at every click, one rubber stamp for weight sharing, max-pool keeps the loudest voice, receptive fields grow, a paper plane takes the ResNet express lane x + f(x), and a volume knob does BatchNorm. Ends with a paintable grid and editable kernel.
